blocks.x: Multimodal AI & Vision-Language Systems as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

Enterprise reality is not text-only: radiology sequences, claim photos, weld seams, shop-floor gauges, satellite plots and engineering drawings carry the signal. We build multimodal systems that combine vision-language models with domain encoders, run them where the data lives (edge, on-prem GPU or cloud), and route their outputs into the operational workflow — a work order, a claim decision, a radiologist's queue — not into a demo dashboard.

Delivery discipline matters more here than model choice: annotation pipelines with inter-rater quality control, class-imbalance handling for rare defects, out-of-distribution monitoring, and clinical or industrial validation protocols. We ship with shadow-mode operation and human-in-the-loop thresholds agreed with the operating function, then tighten autonomy as measured error falls.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
